summary.headline: ADF Foods Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.6% YoY to INR 200.9 crore, its first quarter above INR 200 crore, though container and freight constraints capped conversion.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.6% YoY to INR 200.9 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to INR 39 crore at a 19.4% margin, with PAT of INR 25.3 crore. Standalone revenue grew 16.6% to INR 163.3 crore, but H1 standalone profitability was pressured by elevated freight and logistics costs. Management said order book demand remains strong but shipments were constrained by container and vessel availability, particularly to the Middle East. Management trimmed its FY27 consolidated revenue expectation to about INR 850 crore from INR 900 crore and reiterated high-teens margins.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 163.4 crore, up 22.6% YoY; segment EBITDA margin 25.2%. Management said H1 growth was roughly 24%, with about 60-65% from volume.

segments.name: Ashoka (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue CAGR above 20% over the last five years, driven by South Asian diaspora demand and penetration in core and emerging international markets.

segments.name: Truly Indian (US mainstream)
segments.commentary: Present in more than 3,500 US stores with new listings at Kroger, Meijer and Sprouts; a vegan product was recognised in Whole Foods Market 2027 food trend predictions.

segments.name: Sohna (India)
segments.commentary: Launched A2 cow ghee made with the traditional bilona process, an entry-level product in the everyday kitchen category.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue now expected around INR 850 crore, versus the earlier INR 900 crore target, due to continued container and shipping constraints.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to stay at high-teens levels for the next two quarters, supported by operating leverage as revenue grows about 24-25%.

Surat greenfield facility is still ramping toward targeted operational performance; remaining capex of about INR 40-45 crore planned for Surat, Nadia and Nasik, taking total capex from the INR 145 crore already spent to about INR 190 crore.
Interim dividend declared at 30% of face value.
PLI incentive is in its final year; the company must spend about 2x the incentive on overseas marketing.
capex_capacity: Over the last two and a half years, more than INR 145 crore invested in capacity expansion, funded through internal accruals.
Remaining capex of about INR 40-45 crore for Surat, Nadia and Nasik, implying a total of about INR 190 crore; about INR 60-65 crore of that is for new products.
Management expects asset turn of at least 3x the investment at full capacity.
Sewa (sewer/process) plant: about 15% utilisation of installed lines in Q2; some lines to be installed in Q3; target 35-40% utilisation by fiscal year end.
Surat greenfield facility is making steady progress toward targeted operational performance and adds frozen food capacity.
demand_pricing: Management said demand remains robust; the constraint is shipping capacity, with container and vessel availability still a challenge on certain routes.
Carry-forward shipments continue every month; October saw some improvement on certain routes but not back to pre-war normal.
Middle East: transit times rose from 7-10 days to 35-40 days and freight rates are 7-8x higher; shipments there remain difficult.
Freight and transit disruptions also affect other geographies.
Additional US tariff of about 10% on products; management said lower tariffs or an FTA would help push more volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex remains after the INR 145 crore already spent, and what asset turn should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40-45 crore remains for this year, bringing the total to about INR 190 crore. Management expects asset turn of at least 3x at full capacity, and about INR 60-65 crore is for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand weakening, or is the top line below expectations because of shipping constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is very robust and the constraint is shipping: container and vessel availability, carry-forward shipments, and Middle East disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 19.4% Q2 margin boosted by one-offs such as PLI or tariff refunds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin is sustainable at high-teens levels. PLI is in its final year and must be matched with about 2x in overseas marketing. Insurance recovery was gross-margin neutral, and about INR 3 crore of tariff refund ran through COGS. Insurance cash was received after the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East situation and inventory days improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days are about two weeks above normal. If routes normalise over the next two months, management expects inventory days to return to March levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR 900 crore still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now expects about INR 850 crore, citing container availability and shipping issues in the first two quarters.

risks_watch: Container, vessel and freight availability, plus transit times to the Middle East (35-40 days) and other routes, could keep limiting shipments and conversion of the order book.
Inventory days are running about two weeks above normal, which is a working-capital drag if routes do not normalise.
Gross margin was helped by a roughly INR 3 crore tariff refund that flowed through COGS, so margins need checking for one-offs.
PLI support ends after this year; the company must keep spending on overseas marketing.
Sewa plant utilisation is only about 15% in Q2, with a target of 35-40% by year end.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and on maintaining high-teens margins, but cautious on shipping and guidance: management cut the FY27 revenue expectation to about INR 850 crore and described freight and container conditions as still a challenge.
key_quotes: This represents our highest ever quarterly revenue and marks the first time that ADF has crossed 200 crores in quarterly revenue.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management held high-teens consolidated EBITDA margin for the next two quarters (Q2 at 19.4%, H1 at 18.6%), citing operating leverage as revenue grows about 24-25%, though Q2 included a ~INR 3 crore tariff refund in COGS.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sewa plant has some lines to be installed in Q3 and utilisation is only ~15%, with a 35-40% target by FYE; Surat greenfield is already commissioned and ramping, with ~INR 40-45 crore remaining capex across Surat, Nadia and Nasik.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Processed foods revenue grew 22.6% YoY in Q2 with ~60-65% of H1 growth from volume, and management calls demand very robust; but shipping constraints cap conversion, and FY27 guidance was cut to ~INR 850 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only ~15% at Sewa, so no pressure for new capacity; remaining ~INR 40-45 crore is already planned for Surat, Nadia and Nasik, and management said capital allocation is unchanged, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance was cut to ~INR 850 crore from INR 900 crore on container and shipping constraints, and H1 revenue of INR 368.2 crore needs ~INR 482 crore in H2 to hit the target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The INR 850 crore revenue cut already reflects shipping constraints, but Middle East transit times of 35-40 days, freight 7-8x higher and inventory days ~2 weeks above normal could push revenue below that level if routes do not normalise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About INR 60-65 crore of the remaining capex is for new products, Sohna launched A2 bilona ghee, and Truly Indian is getting new listings at Kroger, Meijer and Sprouts.

rows.label: Inventory days normalisation
rows.why: Inventory days are ~2 weeks above normal; management expects a return to March levels if Middle East routes normalise over the next two months, otherwise it remains a working-capital drag.

rows.label: US tariff relief via lower tariffs or FTA
rows.why: An additional ~10% US tariff weighs on products; management said lower tariffs or an FTA would help push more volume, but no timing was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand and holding high-teens margins, but cautious on shipping and cut FY27 revenue to ~INR 850 crore; analysts probed whether the 19.4% margin had one-offs (PLI, tariff refund, insurance) and whether shipping constraints were hiding weak demand.
